result.topic_en: Euler gives the general formula for q^m when m is odd, notes the coefficient identity for the last term, and explains why his methods fail to determine the sums for orders whose exponent m+n is even.
result.transcription:
SERIES SINGVLARES. 185
II. Casu quo $m$ est numerus impar
$q^m = * + \tfrac{1}{2}(1-\lambda)(n)p^\lambda \begin{matrix}-0(n-1)\\-0(m-1)\end{matrix}\Big\} p \begin{matrix}-2(n-1)\\-2(m-1)\end{matrix}\Big\} p^3 \begin{matrix}-4(n-1)\\-4(m-1)\end{matrix}\Big\} p^5$
$\begin{matrix}-6(n-1)\\-6(m-1)\end{matrix}\Big\} p^7 \ldots\ldots \begin{matrix}-(\lambda-3)(n-1)\\-(\lambda-3)(m-1)\end{matrix}\Big\} p^{\lambda-2}$
Secundum hanc legem terminus vltimum ſequens
fieret $\begin{matrix}(\lambda-1)(n-1)\\(\lambda-1)(m-1)\end{matrix}\Big\} p^\lambda$, vbi notetur ſemper eſſe
$(\lambda-1)(n-1)+(\lambda-1)(m-1) = \lambda(n) = \lambda(m)$.

38. At ſi ordinis exponens $m+n=\lambda$ fuerit
numerus par, hae formulae neutiquam locum habere
poſſunt, cum caſu imparitatis formae $p, p^3, p^5, p^7$ etc.
ob $p^m = p^n$ etiam has pares $p^2, p^4, p^6$ etc. in ſe com-
plectantur, quod autem caſu quo $m+n$ eſt nume-

tur eſt mirandum, quod in ordinibus imparibus

items.english: where it should be noted that always (λ-1)(n-1)+(λ-1)(m-1) = λ(n) = λ(m).

items.quote:
Tres autem methodi hic vſi-
tatae ſummis ordinum parium definiendis non ſuffi-
ciunt, cum etiam tertia pro ordine octauo non
omnes determinationes ſuppeditet.
items.english: The three methods used here do not suffice to determine the sums of even orders, since even the third does not supply all the determinations for the eighth order.

items.quote:
Etſi autem pro
ordinibus quarto et ſexto ſummae ſupra ſunt aſſi-
gnatae, in iis tamen nulla lex perſpicitur, vnde
pro ordinibus ſequentibus coniecturam deducere lice-
ret.
items.english: Although the sums for the fourth and sixth orders were assigned above, no law can be discerned in them from which a conjecture for the following orders could be drawn.

items.quote:
Ratio huius diſcriminis manifeſto in eo eſt ſita,
quod pro ordinibus paribus, binae quaeuis harum
formularum $p^\lambda, p^2, p^4, p^6$ etc. inter ſe comparari
queant, haeque comparationes per methodos noſtras
indicentur; quocirca eae determinationes, quibus
indigemus, deficere ſunt cenſendae.
items.english: The reason for this difference evidently lies in the fact that for even orders any two of these formulas p^λ, p^2, p^4, p^6 etc. can be compared with each other, and these comparisons are what our methods yield; hence the determinations we need must be judged to be lacking.
